$comment: What the package-schema acceptance criterion answers on this tree, per assertion (D-110).
A two-way ratchet: the CI job fails when a run disagrees with this file in either direction.
A1 … A9 are `pass` since T046, which is the transition this file was written for: it stops
being the record of a gap and becomes the guard against regressions. An accidental *red* now
fails the job exactly as an accidental green did — and the green is still the one worth being
careful about, because a change that quietly satisfied an assertion without going through the
composition would show up here as drift rather than as a pass nobody looked at.
Move an entry only in the merge request that earned the move, and never to make a pipeline
pass.
T031 moved A5 to `pass` (an installed package now reaches `resolvedManifestEntries()` and
both composition roots) and corrected A6's and A7's reasons, which had both read `Follows
A5` and stopped being true the moment A5 did.
T033 moved A1, A2, A3 and A4 to `pass` — the whole schema half. A package's migrations and
entities now reach the ORM through the async seam in `src/db/configured-migrations.ts` and
`src/db/configured-entities.ts`.
T032 moved no status and rewrote A5's reason: the assertion now measures the bundles through
`reconcileBundles` and `translation_bundles` rather than reading the files itself, which is
what its own recorded reason named as still missing. A reason that has stopped being true is
drift this file cannot detect — only the status is compared — so it is corrected by hand in
the merge request that made it false, exactly as T031 did for A6 and A7.
T033a/T036 moved no status and rewrote A7's reason, which its own change falsified.
D-157.6(b) narrows the first-boot reconciler's insert population to core plus overlay, so no
boot will ever converge a package and A7's row has exactly one author, `install`.
T053(c) added A10 — a tenth, and the only one recorded `fail`. It is not a schema assertion:
it asks whether the overlay pattern's one customisation seam reaches an owner that has become
a package, which needed no new harness because this one already packs, installs and composes
one. It is red on a single cause, named in its entry, and the entry is the deliverable: the
question stops being open and starts being measured on every merge request.
T046 moved A6 and A7 to `pass`. Neither needed the mechanism its own recorded reason named:
what both needed was for the probe to run the sequence an operator runs. `install` is a
package's only author — of its `module_registrations` row since D-157.6(b), and of its
settings rows through step 2 of the same operation — and no phase installed. Both reasons are
rewritten below to say what the pass now means.

A1.reason: Earned by T033 (P3 option A). The committed migration registry is still a walk of `backend/src` and still contributes no package entry — that is D-119's answer and it does not move. What moved is that the *configured* order is no longer the committed registry: `src/db/configured-migrations.ts` became an async factory that merges it with every installed package's `./migrations` export, tagged `origin: 'external'` so a stranger's stamp cannot join the frozen historical prefix. The probe reports the package's class applied alongside 158 core migrations.

A2.reason: Follows A1, and is kept separate from it on purpose: the table exists because the migration body ran.

A3.reason: The tenant column and the named index are both in `information_schema` as the package's migration declared them — `organization_id uuid` nullable, `acceptance_probe_rows_organization_id_index`. This is the assertion that distinguishes a migration that ran from a row in `mikro_orm_migrations` standing in for one.

A4.reason: Earned by T033. The source-text probe still cannot see a compiled decorator and never will, so the committed entity registry is unchanged; `src/db/configured-entities.ts` merges it at runtime with the entity classes each package's `./backend` export declares. `em.find(AcceptanceProbeRow, {})` returns against the host's own metadata.

A5.reason: Earned by T031 (P1) and **completed by T032 (P2)**, which moved no status and changed what the pass means. `loadPackageModuleEntries` (`src/packages/`) enumerates the instance's `node_modules`, keeps every package carrying `endora.type === "module"` whose install does not link out of the tree it was found under, and both composition roots now call `composeModules([...MODULES, ...overlay, ...packages], …)`. `resolvedManifestEntries()` merges the same discovery, so the module has an identity, its permission is grantable and the palette action resolves in `en` and `pl`. `filePath` is the resolved `package.json`, because `dirname(filePath)` is how the i18n reconciler and the orchestrator find a module's assets and the compiled root export's directory holds no `i18n/`. T032 replaced the assertion's own `loadModuleBundles` read with the platform's path: it runs `reconcileBundles` over the whole resolved set and then reads the action keys back out of `getMergedBundleForLanguage`, which is what the Admin SPA and the command palette serve from. The previous wording recorded exactly this as still outstanding. A package whose bundles the reconciler cannot reach now fails A5 with its `i18n/` sitting in `node_modules`, which is the case the old read could not distinguish from a pass.

A6.reason: Earned by T046, and by a phase rather than by a mechanism. The recorded reason named two causes; the first had been superseded and the second was the whole of it. (1) `composition.ts` reconciling settings from bare-core `REGISTERED_MANIFESTS` is a real defect and is fixed here — the population is now `deploymentShippedEntries(resolvedRegistry)`, the same core-plus-overlay split D-157.6(b) ruled for the first-boot presence insert and the same function, not a second copy of the origin test — but it is **not** what moves this assertion, which was measured: with that fix in and the probe's phases reverted, the run still answers 7 pass / 2 fail. It bites on an **overlay** module, whose presence is converged at boot and which therefore has no `install` to author its settings; `example_overlay` declares an activation control and had no row for it. A package is deliberately still excluded from the boot reconcile: since D-157.6(b) `install` is its only author, and reconciling a stranger's manifest at boot would let a `SettingCodeConflict` in something an operator merely `pnpm add`ed abort the platform's start. (2) The probe read the row before anything had composed or installed. It now runs `boot` — one `composeApp()`, which converges `module_registrations` for what this build ships, so the package's `auth` dependency is installed and the package itself is asserted still absent — and then `install`, in the shape `scripts/install.ts` builds it. The activation Setting exists, `gate-off` flips it and the route answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, `gate-on` flips it back and the route answers again. The operator-axis behaviour behind this pass is held by `test/integration/_lifecycle/package-activation-setting.integration.test.ts`, without a tarball: the row is created at the manifest default, `disable`→`enable` preserves the operator's choice and soft `uninstall`→`install` resets it to the default, for an entry the platform classifies as a package.

A7.reason: Earned by T046, and by nothing of its own: every part of the revert was already settled and the blocker was upstream. Its migration count was settled by T033 (`revertMigrationsFor` takes an injected `MigrationOwnership`, `composition.ts` supplies the merged one, and the empty case refuses rather than warning). Its row has exactly one author, `install`, since D-157.6(b), and T036 taught the CLI to name a package id. What was missing was the call: `uninstall` short-circuited on `already-uninstalled` because no `module_registrations` row for `acceptance_probe` existed, and the probe reached `install` through no phase at all. It now does, and the hard uninstall reverts exactly one migration, drops `acceptance_probe_rows` and leaves the 158 core migrations alone. One thing did change in the uninstall phase itself: its registry was built from an identity map written before `lifecycleParticipant` existed, so the field was silently dropped and the hard uninstall removed the package's schema while leaving its translation bundles and palette actions behind — the one case D-159 §7 records as having no other cure. The entries are handed over unmapped now, the way `composition.ts` hands its own registry over.

A8.reason: Passes today, and must: it measures the harness, not the platform. The tarball install resolves entirely inside the throwaway instance. An A8 that could not pass before Wave 3 would be an assertion nobody could trust after it.

A9.reason: Passes today, and must, for the same reason: A8 refuses the same package consumed by link from inside this repository. If A9 ever fails, A8 has stopped being able to say no and every other assertion is worth less.

A10.reason: **Red, and measured rather than assumed — which is the whole of T053(c).** A per-deployment overlay cannot decorate a registration an installed package owns, and the layer is exactly one: the **order of the arrays in the composition root**. `composeApp` calls `composeModules([...MODULES, ...overlayModuleEntries, ...packageModuleEntries], …)`, and registration runs in array order with no topological pass — so a deployment's overlay module registers *before* the package whose name it wraps, `container.hasRegistration('acceptanceProbeGreeter')` is false, and `ctx.di.decorate` refuses with "nothing is registered under that name. Decoration wraps an existing registration; register order is topological, so the owning module must come first." The refusal is `ModuleCompositionError`-wrapped and takes the whole composition down, so a deployment that tries this does not degrade — it does not boot. Nothing else is wrong: the overlay module was discovered, was composed, and reached `decorate` at all, which is what says `loadOverlayModuleEntries` marked it `overlay: true`. Measured with the two arrays swapped and nothing else changed, A10 answers `pass` — `acceptanceProbeGreeter` resolves to `"overlay:acceptance probe"`, the deployment's wrap delegating into the package's own implementation — so the `overlay: true` exemption over a **package** owner works today and is reached by nobody. The swap is not committed: which array composes last is a ruling about the overlay pattern (the comment above that call already claims "overlay last, so a deployment's decoration wins" as structural, and for a package owner it is not), and a task row that adds an assertion is not where that gets decided. Record the move here in the merge request that earns it.
